concept.name: Process metric
concept.definition: A quantitative measure of how well the trading process was executed - rule-adherence rate, setup-selection grade distribution, slippage versus plan, review completion - independent of whether individual trades won or lost. Process metrics make discipline measurable and correct for outcome bias in self-evaluation.
concept.intuition: P&L tells you what the market did; process metrics tell you what you did.
concept.mechanics: Derived from the journal and execution data: percentage of trades on valid playbook setups, stops honored, planned size used, entries within the trigger window, checklist completion. Tracked weekly and monthly to detect behavioral drift before it shows up in the equity curve.
concept.failure_modes: Metrics get gamed (Goodhart's law): traders contort behavior to hit adherence percentages while hollowing out their meaning. Process metrics also cannot validate the strategy itself - perfect process on zero edge still loses.
concept.misconceptions: Process metrics are not vanity statistics; they are leading indicators because process degradation precedes P&L degradation. They also do not replace outcome metrics - the two are read together.
concept.example: A trader tracks: 94% of trades on playbook setups, 100% of stops honored, average entry slippage 0.04 - and treats a dip in any of them as a warning independent of the month's profit.
